message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and no money left the account). Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) revenue was $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full fiscal 2024 net sales were $391.0B with net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 — figures I confirmed against the SEC 10-K filed 2024-11-01 ($391,035M revenue, $93,736M net income, $6.08 diluted EPS), noting the year included a one-time $10.2B tax charge. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were steady around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the phased Apple Intelligence rollout, so I sized a modest starter position rather than a full allocation. I used the broker quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) as the market reference and set the limit just above the ask for a high-probability fill; I disregarded several search results claiming AAPL traded near $22.30, which were clearly erroneous/spam pages inconsistent with both the broker quote and the news article.
